title: Temurah 21
description: Rabbi Avin bar Kahana’s “forced answer, Babylonian style”; substitutes of a firstborn and a tithe animal, and how firstborn and tithe differ from all other sacrificial animals; the dilemma from the West about blemishing them; ben Antigonus’s Babylonian firstborns and Rabbi Yosei’s three teachings of three elders on one verse; then chapter 3 ends and chapter 4 opens with the sin offerings left to die.
topics: 🤏 “I answer forced answers, Babylonian style”: females born to females until the end of time
🏷️ Substitutes of a firstborn and a tithe animal: eaten in their blemish, never sold by the litra or redeemed
🌍 Firstborn and tithe from outside the Land: “if they came unblemished, they are sacrificed”, and Rabbi Shimon’s reason
🩹 The dilemma from the West: is one liable for blemishing the substitute of a firstborn, or the ninth called tenth?
🇧🇧 Ben Antigonus’s firstborns from Babylonia: Rabbi Yishmael against Rabbi Akiva
📜 Three elders on one verse (Deuteronomy 14:23): second tithe today, firstborns from abroad, eating within the walls, and the “others” on a firstborn past its year
🧱 Derived from the derived: Rabbi Yoḥanan’s rule for sacrificial matters, and “the meat and the blood are one matter”
📖 Hadran: chapter 3, Elu Kodashim, ends; chapter 4, Vlad Ḥatat, opens with the sin offerings that are left to die
