a1.he: עַצְמוֹ — לֹא! הָכָא בְמַאי עָסְקִינַן? כְּגוֹן שֶׁיָּלְדָה נְקֵבָה, וְעַד סוֹף הָעוֹלָם לֹא אוֹלִיד חַד זָכָר?! אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מְשַׁנֵּינָא [לָךְ] שִׁינּוּיֵי דְּחִיקִי בַּבְלָאֵי, כְּגוֹן שֶׁיָּלְדָה נְקֵבוֹת עַד סוֹף הָעוֹלָם.

a2.he: מַתְנִי׳ תְּמוּרַת הַבְּכוֹר וְהַמַּעֲשֵׂר, וְלָדָן וְלַד וְלָדָן עַד סוֹף הָעוֹלָם — הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ כִּבְכוֹר וּכְמַעֲשֵׂר, וְיֵאָכְלוּ בְּמוּמָן לַבְּעָלִים.

a3.he: מָה בֵּין בְּכוֹר וּמַעֲשֵׂר לְבֵין כׇּל הַקֳּדָשִׁים? שֶׁכׇּל הַקֳּדָשִׁים נִמְכָּרִים בָּאִיטְלֵז, וְנִשְׁחָטִין בָּאִיטְלֵז, וְנִשְׁקָלִין בְּלִיטְרָא, חוּץ מִן הַבְּכוֹר וְהַמַּעֲשֵׂר.

a4.he: וְיֵשׁ לָהֶן פִּדְיוֹן, וְלִתְמוּרוֹתֵיהֶן פִּדְיוֹן, חוּץ מִן הַבְּכוֹר וְהַמַּעֲשֵׂר. וּבָאִין מֵחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ, חוּץ מִן הַבְּכוֹר וְהַמַּעֲשֵׂר, שֶׁאִם בָּאוּ תְּמִימִים — יִקְרְבוּ, וְאִם בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין — יֵאָכְלוּ בְּמוּמָן לַבְּעָלִים.

a5.he: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: מָה טַעַם שֶׁהַבְּכוֹר וְהַמַּעֲשֵׂר יֵשׁ לָהֶן פַּרְנָסָה מִמְּקוֹמָן, וּשְׁאָר כׇּל הַקֳּדָשִׁים, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנּוֹלַד בָּהֶם מוּם — הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ בִּקְדוּשָּׁתָן.

a6.he: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רָבָא בַּר רַב עַזָּא: בָּעַן בְּמַעְרְבָא — הַמֵּטִיל מוּם בִּתְמוּרַת בְּכוֹר וּמַעֲשֵׂר מַהוּ? מִי אָמְרִינַן: כֵּיוָן דְּלָא קְרִיבָן — לָא מִיחַיַּיב, אוֹ דִילְמָא: כֵּיוָן דְּקָדְשׁוּ — מִיחַיַּיב?

a7.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וְתִיבְּעֵי לָךְ הַמֵּטִיל מוּם בִּתְשִׁיעִי שֶׁל מַעֲשֵׂר!

a8.he: אֶלָּא מַאי שְׁנָא תְּשִׁיעִי, דְּלָא קָמִיבַּעְיָא לָךְ? דְּרַחֲמָנָא מַעֲטֵיהּ, ״עֲשִׂירִי״ — לְהוֹצִיא הַתְּשִׁיעִי.

a9.he: הָכִי נָמֵי, רַחֲמָנָא מַעֲטִינְהוּ, ״לֹא תִפְדֶּה קֹדֶשׁ הֵם״ — הֵם קְרֵיבִין, וְאֵין תְּמוּרָתָן קְרֵיבָה.

a10.he: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק מַתְנֵי לַהּ הָכִי: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב עַזָּא, בָּעַן בְּמַעְרְבָא: הַמֵּטִיל מוּם בִּתְשִׁיעִי שֶׁל מַעֲשֵׂר מַהוּ? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְתִיבְּעֵי לָךְ הַמֵּטִיל מוּם בִּתְמוּרַת בְּכוֹר וּמַעֲשֵׂר!

a11.he: אֶלָּא מַאי שְׁנָא תְּמוּרַת בְּכוֹר וּמַעֲשֵׂר דְּלָא מִיבַּעְיָא לָךְ? דְּרַחֲמָנָא מַעֲטִינְהוּ, ״קֹדֶשׁ הֵם״ — הֵן קְרֵיבִין וְאֵין תְּמוּרָתָן קְרֵיבָה. תְּשִׁיעִי שֶׁל מַעֲשֵׂר נָמֵי רַחֲמָנָא מַעֲטֵיהּ, ״הָעֲשִׂירִי״ — לְהוֹצִיא אֶת הַתְּשִׁיעִי.

a12.he: וְאִם בָּאוּ תְּמִימִין כּוּ׳. וּרְמִינְהוּ: בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס הֶעֱלָה בְּכוֹרוֹת מִבָּבֶל וְלֹא קִבְּלוּ מִמֶּנּוּ! אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא — רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, הָא — רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא.

a13.he: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים מִשּׁוּם שְׁלֹשָׁה זְקֵנִים, רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר: יָכוֹל יַעֲלֶה אָדָם מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי בִּזְמַן הַזֶּה וְיֹאכְלֶנּוּ בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם?

a14.he: וְדִין הוּא: בְּכוֹר טָעוּן הֲבָאַת מָקוֹם, וּמַעֲשֵׂר טָעוּן הֲבָאַת מָקוֹם. מָה בְּכוֹר אֵינוֹ נֶאֱכָל אֶלָּא בִּפְנֵי הַבַּיִת, אַף מַעֲשֵׂר אֵינוֹ נֶאֱכָל אֶלָּא בִּפְנֵי הַבַּיִת. לֹא, אִם אָמַרְתָּ בִּבְכוֹר — שֶׁכֵּן טָעוּן מַתַּן דָּמִים וְאֵימוּרִים לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ, תֹּאמַר בְּמַעֲשֵׂר דְּלָא?!

a15.he: אָמַרְתָּ: בִּיכּוּרִים טְעוּנִין הֲבָאַת מָקוֹם, וּמַעֲשֵׂר טָעוּן הֲבָאַת מָקוֹם. מָה בִּיכּוּרִים אֵין נֶאֱכָלִין אֶלָּא בִּפְנֵי הַבַּיִת, אַף מַעֲשֵׂר אֵין נֶאֱכָל אֶלָּא בִּפְנֵי הַבַּיִת.

a16.he: מָה לְבִיכּוּרִים, שֶׁכֵּן טְעוּנִין הַנָּחָה, תֹּאמַר בְּמַעֲשֵׂר דְּלָא?!

a17.he: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וְאָכַלְתָּ לִפְנֵי ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ... מַעְשַׂר דְּגָנְךָ וְתִירוֹשְׁךָ וְיִצְהָרֶךָ וּבְכוֹרוֹת בְּקָרְךָ וְצֹאנֶךָ״, הִקִּישׁ מַעֲשֵׂר לִבְכוֹר: מָה בְּכוֹר אֵינוֹ נֶאֱכָל אֶלָּא בִּפְנֵי הַבַּיִת, אַף מַעֲשֵׂר אֵין נֶאֱכָל אֶלָּא בִּפְנֵי הַבַּיִת.

a19.he: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: מִשּׁוּם דְּאִיכָּא לְמֵימַר, מָה לְהַצַּד הַשָּׁוֶה שֶׁבָּהֶן, שֶׁכֵּן יֵשׁ בָּהֶן צַד מִזְבֵּחַ.

a20.he: וּמַאי קָסָבַר? אִי קָסָבַר קְדוּשָּׁה רִאשׁוֹנָה קִידְּשָׁה לִשְׁעָתָהּ וְקִידְּשָׁה לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא, לָא שְׁנָא בְּכוֹר וְלָא שְׁנָא מַעֲשֵׂר בְּנֵי הֲבָאָה נִינְהוּ. וְאִי קָסָבַר קְדוּשָּׁה רִאשׁוֹנָה קִידְּשָׁה לִשְׁעָתָהּ וְלֹא קִידְּשָׁה לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא, אֲפִילּוּ בְּכוֹר נָמֵי תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ!

a21.he: לְעוֹלָם קָסָבַר, קְדוּשָּׁה רִאשׁוֹנָה קִידְּשָׁה לִשְׁעָתָהּ וְלֹא קִידְּשָׁה לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא, וְהָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן — כְּגוֹן שֶׁנִּזְרַק דָּמוֹ שֶׁל בְּכוֹר בִּפְנֵי הַבַּיִת, וְחָרַב הַבַּיִת, וַעֲדַיִין בְּשָׂרוֹ קַיָּים.

a22.he: כֵּיוָן דְּאִי אִיתֵיהּ לְדָם (לא) [לָאו] בַּר זְרִיקָה הוּא, אָתֵי בָּשָׂר יָלֵיף מִדָּם,

b1.he: וְאָתֵי מַעֲשֵׂר וְיָלֵיף מִבְּכוֹר. וּמִי יָלְפִינַן (קֹדֶשׁ) [בְּקָדָשִׁים] מֵהֲדָדֵי? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כׇּל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ לְמֵדִין לָמֵד מִן הַלָּמֵד, חוּץ מִן הַקֳּדָשִׁים שֶׁאֵין לְמֵדִין לָמֵד מִן הַלָּמֵד!

b2.he: מַעֲשֵׂר חוּלִּין הוּא. הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר בָּתַר לָמֵד אָזְלִינַן, אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר בָּתַר מְלַמֵּד אָזְלִינַן, מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר? בָּשָׂר וָדָם חֲדָא מִילְּתָא הִיא.

b3.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: יָכוֹל יַעֲלֶה אָדָם בְּכוֹר מֵחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ לָאָרֶץ בִּזְמַן שֶׁבֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים וְיַקְרִיבֶנּוּ? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וְאָכַלְתָּ לִפְנֵי ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ מַעְשַׂר דְּגָנְךָ וְתִירוֹשְׁךָ וְיִצְהָרֶךָ וּבְכוֹרוֹת בְּקָרְךָ וְצֹאנֶךָ״ — מִמְּקוֹם שֶׁאַתָּה מַעֲלֶה מַעְשַׂר דָּגָן, אַתָּה מַעֲלֶה בְּכוֹר.

b4.he: וּמִמְּקוֹם שֶׁאִי אַתָּה מַעֲלֶה מַעְשַׂר דָּגָן — אִי אַתָּה מַעֲלֶה בְּכוֹר.

b5.he: בֶּן עַזַּאי אוֹמֵר: יָכוֹל (מַעֲלֶה אֶת) [יַעֲלֶה אָדָם] מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי, וְיֹאכְלֶנּוּ בְּכׇל הָרוֹאֶה? וְדִין הוּא: בְּכוֹר טָעוּן הֲבָאַת מָקוֹם, וּמַעֲשֵׂר טָעוּן הֲבָאַת מָקוֹם — מָה בְּכוֹר אֵינוֹ נֶאֱכָל אֶלָּא לִפְנִים מִן הַחוֹמָה, אַף מַעֲשֵׂר אֵינוֹ נֶאֱכָל אֶלָּא לִפְנִים מִן הַחוֹמָה.

b6.he: מָה לִבְכוֹר — שֶׁכֵּן טָעוּן מַתַּן דָּמִים וְאֵימוּרִין לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ, תֹּאמַר בְּמַעֲשֵׂר דְּלָא?! תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וְאָכַלְתָּ לִפְנֵי ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ... מַעְשַׂר דְּגָנְךָ וְתִירוֹשְׁךָ וְיִצְהָרֶךָ וּבְכוֹרוֹת בְּקָרְךָ וְצֹאנֶךָ״ — מַקִּישׁ מַעֲשֵׂר לִבְכוֹר: מָה בְּכוֹר אֵינוֹ נֶאֱכָל אֶלָּא לִפְנִים מִן הַחוֹמָה, אַף מַעֲשֵׂר אֵינוֹ נֶאֱכָל אֶלָּא לִפְנִים מִן הַחוֹמָה.

b7.he: מַאי קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ דְּקָאָמַר ״יָכוֹל״? אָמַרְתָּ הוֹאִיל וּתְנַן: אֵין בֵּין שִׁילֹה לִירוּשָׁלַיִם אֶלָּא שֶׁבְּשִׁילֹה אוֹכְלִין קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים וּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי בְּכׇל הָרוֹאֶה, וּבִירוּשָׁלַיִם לִפְנִים מִן הַחוֹמָה,

b8.he: וְכֵן קׇדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים לִפְנִים מִן הַקְּלָעִים, מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם לַיְתֵי מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי בְּכׇל הָרוֹאֶה? קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.

b9.he: אֲחֵרִים אוֹמְרִים: יָכוֹל יְהֵא בְּכוֹר שֶׁעִבְּרָה שְׁנָתוֹ כִּפְסוּלֵי הַמּוּקְדָּשִׁין, וְיִפָּסֵל?

b10.he: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״מַעְשַׂר דְּגָנְךָ וְתִירוֹשְׁךָ וְיִצְהָרֶךָ״, מַקִּישׁ בְּכוֹר לְמַעֲשֵׂר, מָה מַעֲשֵׂר אֵינוֹ נִפְסָל מִשָּׁנָה לַחֲבֶירְתָּהּ, אַף בְּכוֹר אֵינוֹ נִפְסָל מִשָּׁנָה לַחֲבֶירְתָּהּ.

b11.he: וּלְרַבָּנַן, דְּמַפְּקִי לְהוּ לְטַעְמָא אַחֲרִינָא, מִשָּׁנָה לַחֲבֶירְתָּהּ מְנָא לְהוּ? נָפְקָא לְהוּ מִ״לִּפְנֵי ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ תֹאכְלֶנּוּ שָׁנָה בְשָׁנָה״, לִימֵּד עַל הַבְּכוֹר שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִפְסָל מִשָּׁנָה לַחֲבֶרְתָּהּ.

b12.he: וְלַאֲחֵרִים, לִפְנֵי ״ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ תֹאכְלֶנּוּ שָׁנָה בְשָׁנָה״, מַאי דָּרְשִׁי בֵּיהּ? מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְתַנְיָא: יוֹם אֶחָד מִשָּׁנָה זוֹ, וְיוֹם אֶחָד מִשָּׁנָה אַחֶרֶת, לִימֵּד עַל הַבְּכוֹר שֶׁנֶּאֱכָל לִשְׁנֵי יָמִים וָלָיְלָה אֶחָד.

b13.he: וְרַבָּנַן, דְּנֶאֱכָל לִשְׁנֵי יָמִים וָלָיְלָה אֶחָד מְנָא לְהוּ? אָמַר קְרָא: ״יִהְיֶה לָּךְ כַּחֲזֵה הַתְּנוּפָה״.

b15.he: מַתְנִי׳ וְלַד חַטָּאת, וּתְמוּרַת חַטָּאת, וְחַטָּאת שֶׁמֵּתוּ בְּעָלֶיהָ — יָמוּתוּ, וְשֶׁעִיבְּרָה שְׁנָתָהּ, וְשֶׁאָבְדָה וְנִמְצֵאת בַּעֲלַת מוּם, אִם מִשֶּׁכִּפְּרוּ הַבְּעָלִים — תָּמוּת, וְאֵינָהּ עוֹשָׂה תְּמוּרָה.

messages.text: Continued from 20b: Rabbi Avin bar Kahana ruled that the offspring of a female designated as a guilt offering is itself sacrificed as a burnt offering. Rabbi Avin bar Ḥiyya objected from Rabbi Elazar’s words in the mishna: with the money received for their sale, yes, the owner brings a burnt offering,
but the offspring itself is not sacrificed as a burnt offering.

notes.he: ואע"ג דולד התמורה חזי להקרבה:
notes.en: Itself [not]: even though the offspring of the substitute is fit for sacrifice.

messages.text: What are we dealing with here? It is a case where the female designated as a guilt offering or as the substitute of a guilt offering gave birth to a female, which cannot itself be offered as a guilt offering.

notes.he: הכא במאי עסקינן דיביא בדמיהן כגון דלא חזי להקרבה דנקבה ילדה:
notes.en: What are we dealing with here? That he brings [a burnt offering] with their money, where [the offspring] is not fit for sacrifice, because she gave birth to a female.

messages.text: This is problematic, as the mishna states that the same is true with regard to the offspring of its offspring until the end of time. But could the mishna be referring to a case where until the end of time not even one male was born?

I answer forced answers, in the manner of the Babylonians, and say that the mishna is referring to a case where it gave birth to females, and those females also gave birth to females, until the end of time.
messages.lead: Rabbi Avin bar Kahana said to him in response:

notes.he: כלומר מדקאמר משנינא לך שינויי דחיקי בבלאי מכלל דהוה ידע שינויא אחרינא:
notes.en: What would he have answered him? [A line in Rashi’s text that is not in our printed Gemara.] That is, from his saying “I answer you forced answers, Babylonian style,” it follows that he knew another answer.

notes.he: משנינא לך שינוי דחיקי בבלאי דעיילא פילא בקופא דמחטא [אין] דמתניתין בהכי עסקינן דילדה נקבה עד סוף העולם:
notes.en: I answer you forced answers, Babylonian style, who bring an elephant through the eye of a needle: yes, our mishna deals with a case where she gave birth to a female, [and so on] until the end of the world.

notes.he: דחיקי [כי האי גוונא] מאי הוה יכיל לשנויי בה:
notes.en: And if not for a forced answer [like this one], what could he have answered about it?

notes.he: האי דקתני יפלו דמיהן לנדבה היינו כי ילדה נקבה אבל ילדה זכר יקרב עולה (כדאמינא אנא) [כדאמרן]:
notes.en: He could have answered: what is taught, “their money goes to free-will offerings,” is when she gave birth to a female; but if she gave birth to a male, it is sacrificed as a burnt offering, as we said.

notes.he: מה שאמרו חכמים ויפלו דמיהן לנדבה היינו [עול'] א"כ מה בין דברי רבי אלעזר לחכמים אלא זה יש ביניהם דבזמן שהיא באה חובה לנדבת יחיד כדברי ר' אלעזר טעונה סמיכה ונסכים משלו כשאר קרבן יחיד ואם היה כהן זה שמביאה עבודתה ועורה שלו שאף על פי שאין משמר שלו עובד יכול הוא להקריבה ולהקטירה דכתיב ובא בכל אות נפשו ושרת ועורה יהיה שלו כדכתיב עור העולה אשר הקריב לכהן לו יהיה ובזמן שהיא באה נדבה לעולה נדבת צבור אין סומך עליה דאין קרבן צבור טעון סמיכה ואינו מביא עליה נסכים משלו אלא משל צבור ואע"פ שהוא כהן בעל ולד תמורה אשם זה אינו יכול לעובדה אלא עבודתה ועורה לאנשי משמר העובד:
notes.en: [A note on the mishna of 20b.] But even in a free-will offering it is a burnt offering: what the Sages said, “their money goes to free-will offerings,” means a [burnt offering]. If so, what is the difference between the words of Rabbi Elazar and the Sages? Only this: when it comes as an obligation, as an individual’s free-will offering, as Rabbi Elazar says, it requires leaning [of hands] and libations from his own [means], like any individual’s offering; and if the one who brings it is a priest, its service and its hide are his. Even though it is not his priestly watch that is serving, he may sacrifice it and burn it, as it is written: “And he shall come with all the desire of his soul… and he shall minister” (Deuteronomy 18:6–7), and its hide is his, as it is written: “The hide of the burnt offering which he has offered shall be the priest’s, it shall be his” (Leviticus 7:8). But when it comes as a free-will offering for the communal free-will burnt offerings, he does not lean on it, since a communal offering does not require leaning, and he does not bring libations for it from his own but from the community’s. And even if the owner of this offspring of the substitute of a guilt offering is a priest, he cannot perform its service; rather, its service and its hide belong to the men of the serving watch.

messages.text: Rashi and Rabbeinu Gershom read a further question here that is not in our printed text: had he not given a forced answer, what could he have answered? Rabbeinu Gershom answers: the mishna’s “their money goes to free-will offerings” refers to a female offspring, while a male is itself sacrificed as a burnt offering.
Mishna

With regard to the substitute of a firstborn offering and the substitute of an animal tithe offering, and the offspring of those substitutes and the offspring of their offspring until the end of time, the halakhic status of these animals is like that of a firstborn offering and like that of an animal tithe offering in that they must be treated with sanctity:

notes.he: לכל קדושת בכור ומעשר שלא ימכרו באיטליז לאחר שנפל בהן מום ונפדו:
notes.en: MISHNA. These are like a firstborn and a tithe animal: in all the sanctity of a firstborn and a tithe animal, that they are not sold in the butchers’ market after a blemish befell them and they were redeemed.

messages.text: They graze until they become blemished, and at that point they may be eaten in their blemished state, the substitute of the firstborn by the priests and the substitute of the animal tithe by their owners. They are not sacrificed upon the altar like the original firstborn and animal tithe offerings.

notes.he: בלא פדיון כבכור ומעשר שאין בהן פדיון דכתיב בהו לא יפדה ולא יגאל:
notes.en: And they are eaten in their blemish by the owners: without redemption, like a firstborn and a tithe animal, which have no redemption, since it is written of them “you shall not redeem” (Numbers 18:17) and “it shall not be redeemed” (Leviticus 27:33).

messages.text: What is the practical difference between a firstborn offering and an animal tithe offering and all the other sacrificial animals? The difference is that all the other sacrificial animals that were blemished and redeemed are sold in the butchers’ market [ba’itliz], and slaughtered in the butchers’ market, and weighed and sold by the litra, in the manner that non-sacred meat is slaughtered and sold.

notes.he: משום דריוח שלהן להקדש חוץ מבכור ומעשר שהנאתן לבעלים הילכך אין מזלזלין בהן:
notes.en: For all sacrificial animals are sold in the butchers’ market: because their profit goes to the Temple treasury; except for the firstborn and the tithe animal, whose benefit goes to the owners. Therefore we do not treat them with disrespect.

messages.text: This is the case with regard to all consecrated animals except for the firstborn and animal tithe offerings, which are sold only from the home and not by the litra.

notes.he: מפני שאין הנאתן להקדש במכירתם דדמי בכור לכהן ודמי מעשר לבעלים ומשום הנאה דידהו לא מזלזלינן בקדשים:
notes.en: Except for the firstborn and the tithe animal: because the benefit from their sale does not go to the Temple treasury, since the money for a firstborn goes to the priest and the money for a tithe animal goes to the owners, and for the sake of their benefit we do not treat sacred things with disrespect.

messages.text: And in addition, all sacrificial animals that became blemished are subject to redemption through sale, at which point the money becomes sacred and the animal becomes non-sacred, and their substitutes are also subject to redemption through sale. This is true for all consecrated animals, except for the firstborn and animal tithe offerings, which are not subject to redemption.

notes.he: נפל בהן מום בבכור ומעשר אינו יכול להוציאן מקדושה דבבכור כתיב לא תפדה ובמעשר כתיב לא יגאל:
notes.en: If a blemish befell a firstborn or a tithe animal, one cannot take them out of their sanctity, since of the firstborn it is written “you shall not redeem” (Numbers 18:17) and of the tithe animal it is written “it shall not be redeemed” (Leviticus 27:33).

messages.text: And all sacrificial animals come to be sacrificed in the Temple even from outside of Eretz Yisrael, except for the firstborn and animal tithe offerings, which should not be brought from outside Eretz Yisrael ab initio. But if they came unblemished, they are sacrificed in the Temple like a regular firstborn or animal tithe offering coming from Eretz Yisrael; and if they are blemished animals, they may be eaten in their blemished state, the firstborns by the priests and the animal tithes by their owners.

notes.he: שאין באין לכתחלה מחוצה לארץ כשאר כל הקדשים:
notes.en: Except for the firstborn and the tithe animal: which do not come ab initio from outside the Land, as all other sacrificial animals do.

notes.he: ובאין מחוצה לארץ לארץ להקריב חוץ מן הבכור ומעשר שאין באין ואף על פי כן אם באו תמימין דיעבד בכור ומעשר יקרבו ואם בעלי מומין יאכלו לבעלים בלא פדיון] (מתני') ואמר רבי שמעון מה טעם בכור ומעשר אין באין מחוצה לארץ (לפי שיש) [לכתחילה מפני שבכור ומעשר] יש להן פרנסה במקומן [שיכול לפרנסן בחוצה לארץ עד שעה] שיפול בהן מום קבוע ולאלתר כשיפול בהן מום יכול לאוכלן בלא פדיון הילכך אין צריך להעלותן ושאר כל הקדשים אין להן פרנסה בחוצה לארץ שיהו ניתרין לאלתר כשיפול בהן מום בלא פדיון אלא צריכין פדיון הילכך הרי הן בקדושתן וחמירי מבכור ומעשר הילכך באין מחוצה לארץ:
notes.en: And they come from outside the Land to the Land to be sacrificed, except for the firstborn and the tithe animal, which do not come; and even so, if they came unblemished, after the fact, the firstborn and tithe animal are sacrificed, and if blemished they are eaten by the owners without redemption. And Rabbi Shimon said: what is the reason a firstborn and a tithe animal do not come from outside the Land [ab initio]? Because a firstborn and a tithe animal have provision in their place: one can sustain them outside the Land until a permanent blemish befalls them, and as soon as a blemish befalls them one can eat them without redemption. Therefore one need not bring them up. But all other sacrificial animals have no such provision outside the Land, that they become permitted as soon as a blemish befalls them without redemption; rather, they require redemption. Therefore they remain in their sanctity and are more stringent than a firstborn and a tithe animal, and so they come from outside the Land.

messages.text: What is the reason for this last difference between them? It is that the firstborn and animal tithe offerings have a remedy in their place outside Eretz Yisrael, as they can graze until they become blemished and then can be eaten there. It is not necessary to bring them to Eretz Yisrael in order to eat them.

notes.dh: שהבכור והמעשר יש להן פרנסה במקומן
notes.he: יש להן תקנה במקומן שירעו עד שיסתאבו ויאכלו במומם לבעלים ושאר כל הקדשים אע"פ שנפל בהן מום הרי הן בקדושתן וצריך אתה לפדותן ולהעלות דמיהן ולהקריבן והואיל וסופו להקריב דמיהן יעלו הן עצמן ויקרבו:
notes.en: For the firstborn and the tithe animal have provision in their place: they have a remedy in their place, that they graze until they become blemished and are eaten in their blemish by the owners. But all other sacrificial animals, even though a blemish befell them, remain in their sanctity, and you must redeem them, bring up their money and sacrifice [with it]; and since in the end their money will be sacrificed, let them themselves be brought up and sacrificed.

messages.text: But with regard to all other sacrificial animals, even if a blemish develops in them, these animals remain in their sanctity, and one must redeem them and bring another offering with the money of their redemption. Therefore, when they are unblemished it is proper to bring these animals themselves to Eretz Yisrael.

messages.caption: The mishna’s three differences between firstborn and tithe animals and all other sacrificial animals, with Rabbi Shimon’s reason.

messages.text: Gemara
they inquired in the West, Eretz Yisrael: What is the halakha with regard to one who inflicts a blemish on the substitute of a firstborn offering or on the substitute of an animal tithe offering?
messages.lead: With regard to the status of the substitute of firstborn and animal tithe offerings that was discussed in the mishna, Rava bar Rav Azza said that

notes.dh: המטיל מום בתמורת בכור ומעשר מהו
notes.he: בפ' כל המנחות באות מצה (מנחות דף נו:) פליגי תנאי במטיל מום בבעל מום איכא למ"ד לוקה ואיכא למ"ד אינו לוקה והך בעיא דהכא לתרוייהו אפילו למ"ד התם לוקה משום דחזיא להקרבה קודם המום אבל הני דלא חזיא לעולם להקרבה לא לקי או לא שנא ולמ"ד התם אינו לוקה היינו משום דמעיקרא נמי היה בו מום אבל הכא דמעיקרא היה תם לקי או לא שנא:
notes.en: One who inflicts a blemish on the substitute of a firstborn or a tithe animal, what is the law? In the chapter Kol HaMenaḥot Ba’ot Matza (Menaḥot 56b) tanna’im disagree about one who inflicts a blemish on an animal that is already blemished: one says he is flogged and one says he is not. And this dilemma here arises according to both. Even according to the one who says there that he is flogged, that is because there the animal was fit for sacrifice before the blemish; but these, which are never fit for sacrifice, perhaps he is not flogged, or perhaps it makes no difference. And according to the one who says there that he is not flogged, that is because from the outset it already had a blemish; but here, where it was unblemished at the outset, perhaps he is flogged, or perhaps it makes no difference.

notes.dh: הטיל מום בתמורת בכור ומעשר מהו
notes.he: [חומרן דאמרן] המטיל מום (בבהמת) [בשאר] קדשים עובר משום חמשה לאוין הכי מאי מי אמרינן כיון דלא קרבי דכתיב לא תפדה קדש הם הם קרבין ואין תמורתן קרבין ויליף מעשר העברה העברה מבכור והילכך לא מיחייב או דילמא כיון דקדשן כדכתיב והיה הוא ותמורתו יהיה קדש מיחייב:
notes.en: One who inflicts a blemish on the substitute of a firstborn or a tithe animal, what is the law? [Their stringency, which we mentioned:] one who inflicts a blemish on [other] sacrificial animals transgresses five prohibitions. Here, what is the law? Do we say that since they are not sacrificed, as it is written “you shall not redeem; they are holy” (Numbers 18:17), “they” are sacrificed but their substitutes are not, and the tithe animal is derived from the firstborn by the verbal analogy of “passing” and “passing,” and therefore he is not liable? Or perhaps, since they are sanctified, as it is written “then it and its substitute shall be holy” (Leviticus 27:10), he is liable?

messages.text: Do we say that since they are not sacrificed on the altar like the actual firstborn or animal tithe offering, one who does this is not liable, as the prohibition against inflicting a blemish on a sacrificial animal applies only when one thereby disqualifies the animal from the altar, and that is not the case here; or perhaps since they are sanctified, he is liable for inflicting a blemish?

notes.he: מלקות משום כל מום לא יהיה בו:
notes.en: GEMARA. He is not liable: to lashes, on account of “there shall be no blemish in it” (Leviticus 22:21).

messages.text: And let the dilemma be raised in a case of one who inflicts a blemish on other sacrificial animals, such as the ninth animal counted while selecting the animal tithe offering, which was mistakenly declared to be the tenth. This animal is consecrated in that one is prohibited to work it or shear it until it becomes blemished, but it may not be sacrificed upon the altar.
messages.quote: one who inflicts a blemish on the substitute of a firstborn

notes.he: כגון קרא לט' עשירי דקדש ואינו קרב כדאמרינן בשילהי בכורות (דף ס.) התשיעי נאכל במומו:
notes.en: And let the dilemma be raised about the ninth of the tithe: for example, where he called the ninth “tenth,” which is sacred but is not sacrificed, as we say at the end of Bekhorot (60a): the ninth is eaten in its blemish.

notes.dh: ותיבעי ליה [מטיל מום] בתשיעי של מעשר
notes.he: דלא קרב כדתנן קרא לתשיעי עשירי ולעשירי תשיעי ולאחד עשר עשירי שלשתן מקודשין התשיעי נאכל במומו לבעלים והעשירי מעשר והאחד עשר קרב שלמים אבל התשיעי לא קרב [אלא מאי שנא כו']:
notes.en: And let the dilemma be raised about [one who inflicts a blemish on] the ninth of the tithe, which is not sacrificed, as we learned: if he called the ninth “tenth,” the tenth “ninth,” and the eleventh “tenth,” all three are consecrated; the ninth is eaten in its blemish by the owners, the tenth is the tithe animal, and the eleventh is sacrificed as a peace offering. But the ninth is not sacrificed. [Rather, what is different, and so on.]

messages.text: Rather, what is different about the ninth animal, which one called the tenth, that you did not raise the dilemma about it? It is because the Merciful One excluded it, with the verse: “The tenth shall be holy to the Lord”, which serves to exclude from the altar the ninth that was mistakenly declared to be the tenth. One may derive from here that one who inflicts a blemish upon this ninth animal is not liable.

verse.he: וְכׇל־מַעְשַׂר בָּקָר וָצֹאן כֹּל אֲשֶׁר־יַעֲבֹר תַּחַת הַשָּׁבֶט הָעֲשִׂירִי יִהְיֶה־קֹּדֶשׁ לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: All tithes of the herd or flock—of all that passes under the shepherd’s staff, every tenth one—shall be holy to GOD.

notes.he: שלא יקרב וכיון דאינו קרב פשיטא לן דלא מיחייב המטיל בו מום הכא נמי כו':
notes.en: To exclude the ninth: that it is not sacrificed. And since it is not sacrificed, it is obvious to us that one who inflicts a blemish on it is not liable. Here too, and so on.

messages.text: Here, too, with regard to the substitute of a firstborn, the Merciful One excluded it from the altar: “But the firstborn…you shall not redeem; they are holy”. This indicates that they, the firstborns themselves, are sacrificed, but their substitute is not sacrificed, and it may be derived from here that one is also not liable for inflicting a blemish upon the substitute of a firstborn.

verse.he: אַךְ בְּכוֹר־שׁוֹר אוֹ־בְכוֹר כֶּשֶׂב אוֹ־בְכוֹר עֵז לֹא תִפְדֶּה קֹדֶשׁ הֵם אֶת־דָּמָם תִּזְרֹק עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּחַ וְאֶת־חֶלְבָּם תַּקְטִיר אִשֶּׁה לְרֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: But the firstlings of cattle, sheep, or goats may not be redeemed; they are consecrated. You shall dash their blood against the altar, and turn their fat into smoke as an offering by fire for a pleasing odor to GOD.

messages.text: they inquired in the West, Eretz Yisrael: In the case of one who inflicts a blemish upon the ninth animal counted while selecting the animal tithe offering, what is the halakha?
messages.lead: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak teaches that statement in this way, in the opposite manner to the previous version: Rav Aḥa, son of Rav Azza, said that

messages.text: And let the dilemma be raised with regard to one who inflicts a blemish upon the substitute of a firstborn offering or the substitute of an animal tithe offering.
messages.quote: one who inflicts a blemish upon the ninth

messages.text: Rather, what is different about the substitute of a firstborn or the substitute of an animal tithe that you did not raise the dilemma about them? It is because the Merciful One excluded them, as it is stated: “They are holy,” which indicates that they themselves are sacrificed, but their substitutes are not sacrificed.

With regard to the ninth animal counted while selecting the animal tithe as well, the Merciful One excluded it, as it is stated: “The tenth,” which serves to exclude from the altar the ninth that was mistakenly declared to be the tenth.

§ The mishna teaches that although the firstborn and animal tithe offerings should not be brought from outside Eretz Yisrael ab initio, if they came unblemished, they may be sacrificed. With regard to this issue, the Gemara raises a contradiction:
messages.quote: if they came unblemished, they are sacrificed

messages.text: There was an incident where ben Antigonus brought up firstborn animals from Babylonia in order to sacrifice them and they did not accept them in the Temple.

notes.he: וקשיא אמתני' דקתני אם באו תמימים יקרבו:
notes.en: Ben Antigonus, and they did not accept them from him: this is difficult for our mishna, which teaches: if they came unblemished, they are sacrificed.

notes.he: בן (אטיטס) [אנטיגנוס] העלה בכורות ולא קבלו ממנו אפילו דאיעבד:
notes.en: Ben Antigonus brought up firstborns and they did not accept them from him: even after the fact.

messages.text: That is not difficult: This statement in the mishna is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yishmael, while this case of ben Antigonus is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Akiva.

notes.he: (בסיפא אתיא):
notes.en: This is Rabbi Yishmael, and so on: (it is explained below).

notes.he: הא דקתני ואם באו תמימים יקרבו [כר' ישמעאל] דמקיש לקמן מעשר שני לבכור מה בכור אין נאכל אלא בפני הבית מכלל דאפילו בכור חוצה לארץ יאכל לפני הבית והא דקאמר ולא קבלו ממנו [היינו] כר' עקיבא דמקיש לקמן בכור למעשר שני מה מעשר שני אינו בא אלא מן הארץ דכתיב לא תוכל לאכל בשעריך וכו' אף בכור נמי אינו בא אלא מן הארץ:
notes.en: It is not difficult: what it teaches, “if they came unblemished, they are sacrificed,” [is Rabbi Yishmael’s view], who below juxtaposes second tithe to the firstborn: just as a firstborn is eaten only in the presence of the Temple. It follows that even a firstborn from outside the Land is eaten in the presence of the Temple. And what it says, “they did not accept it from him,” [is] Rabbi Akiva’s view, who below juxtaposes the firstborn to second tithe: just as second tithe comes only from the Land, as it is written “you may not eat within your gates…” (Deuteronomy 12:17), so too a firstborn comes only from the Land.

messages.text: As it is taught in a baraita that Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Yishmael disagreed over this matter:
Three matters in the name of three elders: Rabbi Yishmael, Rabbi Akiva, and Ben Azzai, each of whom issued a different statement with regard to a firstborn and second tithe.

notes.he: רבי ישמעאל ור"ע ובן עזאי:
notes.en: Three elders: Rabbi Yishmael, Rabbi Akiva and ben Azzai.

notes.he: ר' ישמעאל ור' עקיבא ובן עזאי. בכור טעון הבאת מקום דכתיב והבאתם שמה עולותיכם וזבחיכם כו' מה בכור אינו נאכל אלא בפני הבית כשהיה דמו קרב למזבח אף מעשר אין נאכל אלא בפני הבית ובזמן שאין בית אין נאכל (אלא) אפי' בירושלים בכורים יוכיחו שאין בהן מתן דמים ואימורין וטעונין הבאת מקום ומעשר טעון הבאת מקום מה בכורים אין נאכלין אלא בפני הבית דכתיב בהו והניחו אצל מזבח:
notes.en: In the name of three elders: Rabbi Yishmael, Rabbi Akiva and ben Azzai. A firstborn requires bringing to the place, as it is written: “And there you shall bring your burnt offerings and your sacrifices…” (Deuteronomy 12:6). Just as a firstborn is eaten only in the presence of the Temple, when its blood was offered on the altar, so too [second] tithe is eaten only in the presence of the Temple, and when there is no Temple it is not eaten, even in Jerusalem. Let first fruits prove it: they have no placing of blood and sacrificial portions, yet they require bringing to the place, and tithe requires bringing to the place; just as first fruits are eaten only in the presence of the Temple, since it is written of them that they are set down beside the altar.

messages.text: One might have thought that a person may bring up second tithe in the present day to Jerusalem and eat it in Jerusalem.

But the opposite conclusion should be derived through logical inference from the halakha of a firstborn: A firstborn requires that it be brought to a specific place, i.e., Jerusalem, and second tithe requires that it be brought to a specific place. Just as a firstborn is eaten only in the presence of the Temple, so too, second tithe is eaten only in the presence of the Temple.

notes.he: בכור ומעשר ובכורים דטעונין הבאת מקום דכתיב (דברים י״ב:ה׳-ו׳) והבאתם שמה עולותיכם וגו' ותרומת ידכם אלו בכורים:
notes.en: A firstborn, tithe and first fruits require bringing to the place, as it is written: “And there you shall bring your burnt offerings… and the teruma of your hand” (Deuteronomy 12:5–6); these are the first fruits.

notes.he: כדמפרש לקמיה דבעי מתן דמים ואימורין למזבח:
notes.en: Just as a firstborn is not eaten, and so on: as it explains below, since it requires placing the blood and sacrificial portions on the altar.

messages.text: This comparison can be refuted: No, if you said that this is true with regard to a firstborn, that it may be eaten only in the presence of the Temple, as it requires placing the blood and sacrificial portions of the offering upon the altar, shall you also say that this is the case with regard to second tithe, for which this is not required?

Rather, perhaps you will say that the halakha of eating second tithe in Jerusalem in the present is derived from a comparison to first fruits: First fruits require that they be brought to a specific place, i.e., Jerusalem, and second tithe requires that they be brought to a specific place. Just as first fruits may be eaten only in the presence of the Temple, so too, second tithe may be eaten only in the presence of the Temple.

notes.dh: בכורים אינן נאכלין אלא בפני הבית
notes.he: דכתיב (שם כו) והנחתו לפני ה' אלהיך:
notes.en: First fruits are eaten only in the presence of the Temple: as it is written: “And you shall set it down before the Lord your God” (Deuteronomy 26:10).

messages.text: But this comparison is also flawed, as what is unique about first fruits? They are unique in that they require placement before the altar, as it is stated: “And the priest shall take the basket out of your hand, and set it down before the altar of the Lord your God”. Perhaps it is for this reason that they must be eaten in the presence of the Temple. Shall you say that this is also the case with regard to second tithe, which is not obligated in placement before the altar?

verse.he: וְלָקַח הַכֹּהֵן הַטֶּנֶא מִיָּדֶךָ וְהִנִּיחוֹ לִפְנֵי מִזְבַּח יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ׃
verse.en: The priest shall take the basket from your hand and set it down in front of the altar of the ETERNAL your God.

notes.he: לפני המזבח דכתיב והנחתו לפני ה' אלהיך:
notes.en: Placement: before the altar, as it is written: “And you shall set it down before the Lord your God.”

messages.text: The verse states with regard to second tithe: “And you shall eat before the Lord your God in the place that He shall choose to cause His name to dwell there, the tithe of your grain, of your wine, and of your oil, and the firstborn of your cattle and sheep”.

verse.he: וְאָכַלְתָּ לִפְנֵי ׀ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בַּמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר־יִבְחַר לְשַׁכֵּן שְׁמוֹ שָׁם מַעְשַׂר דְּגָנְךָ תִּירֹשְׁךָ וְיִצְהָרֶךָ וּבְכֹרֹת בְּקָרְךָ וְצֹאנֶךָ לְמַעַן תִּלְמַד לְיִרְאָה אֶת־יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ כׇּל־הַיָּמִים׃
verse.en: You shall consume the tithes of your new grain and wine and oil, and the firstlings of your herds and flocks, in the presence of the ETERNAL your God, in the place where [God] will choose to establish the divine name, so that you may learn to revere the ETERNAL your God forever.

messages.text: This verse compares second tithe to the firstborn: Just as a firstborn is eaten only in the presence of the Temple, so too, second tithe is eaten only in the presence of the Temple. This concludes the statement of Rabbi Yishmael.

But let the inference return and compare second tithe to both the firstborn and first fruits together, and let the halakha of second tithe be derived by analogy from the common element [bema hatzad] of the two sources: Just as the firstborn and first fruits both require that they be brought to a specific place and are not eaten in the present time, so too, second tithe, which also requires that it must be brought to a specific place, should not be eaten in the present time.

notes.he: למה לי קרא ליהדר דינא ולימא בכור יוכיח וחזר הדין הצד השוה שבהן שטעונין הבאת מקום ואינן נאכלין אלא בפני הבית אף אני אביא מעשר:
notes.en: And let the inference return, and so on: why do I need a verse? Let the inference return and say: let the firstborn prove it, and the inference returns: the common element of them is that they require bringing to the place and are eaten only in the presence of the Temple; so too I will bring tithe [under that rule].

notes.he: ולמה ליה קרא למילף ניהדר דינא וניתי ונילף במה הצד ונימא הכי כיון דאמר מה לבכורים שכן טעונין הנחה נימא בכור יוכיח שאין טעון הנחה אף אני אביא מעשר מה לבכור שכן טעון מתן דמים בכורים יוכיחו וחזר הדין לא ראי הצד השוה כו' שכן יש בהן צד מזבח בכורים הנחה ובכור מתן דמים תאמר במעשר שני שאין בה צד מזבח הילכך איצטריך קרא לאקוש' למעשר]:
notes.en: And why does he need a verse to derive it? Let the inference return and come, and derive it by the common element, saying thus: since he said, “What about first fruits, which require placement?” let us say: let the firstborn prove it, which does not require placement, and I too will bring tithe. “What about the firstborn, which requires placing of blood?” Let first fruits prove it. And the inference returns: the aspect of this is not like the aspect of that, and so on. [Rav Ashi answers:] since they have an aspect of the altar, placement for first fruits and placing of blood for the firstborn; will you say so of second tithe, which has no aspect of the altar? Therefore a verse was needed to juxtapose [it] to tithe.

messages.text: The halakha of second tithe cannot be derived in this manner, because it can be said: What is notable about the common element of these cases? They are notable in that they have an aspect of their halakha that involves the altar: A firstborn must have its blood and sacrificial portions placed upon the altar, and first fruits must be placed before the altar, whereas no obligation with regard to the altar applies to the second tithe at all.
messages.quote: be derived by analogy from the common element

messages.text: According to Rabbi Yishmael, a firstborn is not eaten in the present day, but with regard to second tithe he is uncertain about the halakha. And what does he hold?

notes.he: דפשיטא ליה דבכור אינו נאכל ומעשר שני מספקא ליה:
notes.en: And what does he hold? For it is obvious to him that a firstborn is not eaten, while second tithe is a doubt to him.

messages.text: If he holds that the initial consecration both sanctified Jerusalem for its time and sanctified Jerusalem forever, including the period after the destruction of the Temple, then a firstborn is no different and second tithe is no different, as both are capable of being brought to Jerusalem: In the case of the firstborn, an altar may be built upon which it may be offered, while second tithe may be eaten in Jerusalem, and the presence of the Temple is not required for either one.

notes.he: תרוייהו בכור ומעשר בני הבאה נינהו ויקריבום הואיל והשתא נמי קדושה היא ירושלים להקריב:
notes.en: And sanctified it for the future: both of them, firstborn and tithe, can be brought, and let them sacrifice it, since now too Jerusalem is sacred for sacrificing.

notes.dh: אי קסבר קדושה ראשונה קדשה לשעתה וקדשה לעתיד לבא בכור נמי נייתי
notes.he: פרש"י בזבחים (דף קז:) דלמ"ד קדשה לעתיד לבא מקריבין אע"פ שאין בית וא"ת והא בעינן מזבח וליכא וי"ל דפריך מבכור שנשחט ונזרק דמו קודם שחרב הבית דאין חסר אלא אכילה לפנים מן החומה דומיא דמעשר אי נמי י"ל דפריך הכי בכור נמי נייתי ויבנה מזבח ואי קסבר לא קדשה לעתיד לבא בכור נמי תיבעי ה"ג רש"י וקשה דלמ"ד לא קדשה לעתיד לבא אין קדושה בירושלים יותר משאר ערים ועוד דאמר פ' בתרא דזבחים (ג"ז שם) דלמאן דאמר לא קדשה לעתיד לבא מעשר שני נאכל בכל ערי ישראל ויש לתרץ מיהא קושיא שניה דמיירי הכא במעשר שנזרע קודם שחרב הבית שהיה טעון הבאה בירושלים דבההיא לא אמר דנאכל בכל ערי ישראל:
notes.en: If he holds that the initial consecration sanctified for its time and sanctified for the future, let him bring a firstborn too: Rashi explained in Zevaḥim (107b) that according to the one who says it sanctified for the future, one may sacrifice even though there is no Temple. And if you ask: but we need an altar, and there is none? One can answer that it challenges from a firstborn that was slaughtered and whose blood was sprinkled before the Temple was destroyed, which lacks only eating within the wall, like tithe. Alternatively, one can answer that it challenges thus: let him bring a firstborn too and build an altar. “And if he holds it did not sanctify for the future, let him be in doubt about the firstborn too”: so Rashi reads. And it is difficult: according to the one who says it did not sanctify for the future, there is no more sanctity in Jerusalem than in other cities. And further, it says in the last chapter of Zevaḥim (ibid.) that according to the one who says it did not sanctify for the future, second tithe is eaten in all the cities of Israel. One can resolve at least the second difficulty: here it deals with tithe that was sown before the Temple was destroyed, which required bringing to Jerusalem, and of that it was not said that it is eaten in all the cities of Israel.

notes.he: ומאי קסבר ר' ישמעאל אי קסבר כר' יהושע קדוש' ראשונה שקידשה [יהושע] קידשה נמי לעתיד לבוא אפילו לאחר חרבן אפילו בכור נמי נייתי השתא בירושלים ויאכלנו שם:
notes.en: And what does Rabbi Yishmael hold? If he holds like Rabbi Yehoshua, that the initial consecration that [Joshua] made sanctified also for the future, even after the destruction, then let him bring a firstborn too now in Jerusalem and eat it there.

messages.text: And if he holds that the initial consecration sanctified Jerusalem for its time but did not sanctify Jerusalem forever, and he is still uncertain about the status of second tithe, then raise the dilemma even with regard to the firstborn.

notes.he: ואפילו הכי מספקא ליה ממעשר תיבעי ליה נמי בכור ואמאי יליף מעשר שני מבכור:
notes.en: And if it did not sanctify it for the future, and even so he is in doubt about tithe, let him be in doubt about the firstborn too. And why does he derive second tithe from the firstborn?

notes.he: אפילו מעשר לפשוט ליה דלא נייתי:
notes.en: And if he holds that it did not sanctify [for the future], then even for tithe let him resolve that it is not brought.

messages.text: Actually, he holds that the initial consecration sanctified Jerusalem for its time but did not sanctify it forever, and here we are dealing with a case where the blood of a firstborn offering was sprinkled upon the altar before the Temple was destroyed, and then the Temple was destroyed, but its flesh was still in existence.

notes.he: ודקשיא מאי שנא בכור דפשיטא ליה בכי האי בכור עסקינן שנזרק דמו בפני הבית וחרב כו' ויליף בשר מדם דכי היכי דאי הוה דם השתא לא היה נזרק דלא קידשה לעתיד לבא בשר נמי לא יאכל:
notes.en: Actually, it did not sanctify for the future: and as for your difficulty, what is different about the firstborn, that it is obvious to him? We are dealing with a firstborn like this, whose blood was sprinkled in the presence of the Temple and [the Temple] was destroyed, and so on; and he derives the meat from the blood: just as, if the blood were here now, it would not be sprinkled, since it did not sanctify for the future, so too the meat is not eaten.

notes.dh: הכי גריס רש"י לעולם קסבר לא קדשה לעתיד לבא
notes.he: וקשה דאם כן למה לי האי טעמא דאיתקש בשר לדם תיפוק ליה דנפסל ביוצא דכמי שאין לו חומה דמי ועוד דאמר בזבחים (דף ס.) מזבח שנפגם אין אוכלין בגינו קדשים קלים ומפיק ליה מהאי טעמא דאיתקש בשרו לדמו והכא אמר דהך היקשא דבשר לדם הוי למ"ד לא קדשה לעתיד לבא לכן נראה לר"י דה"ג אי קסבר לא קדשה לעתיד לבא מעשר שני לא לייתי ובמעשר שנזרע קודם שחרב הבית כדפ"ל וה"ג לעולם קסבר קדושה ראשונה קדשה לשעתה וקדשה לעתיד לבא ודקשיא לך בכור נמי לייתי הכא במאי עסקינן שנזרק דמו לפני הבית וחרב הבית כו' והשתא מיתרצו כל קושיין ודקדק מורי בשלמא בכור שנזרק דמו לפני הבית דאינו נאכל אלא בפני הבית כדמפרש גמרא דאיתקש בשר לדם אבל בכורים שהיה להם הנחה לפני הבית מ"ט אין נאכלין אלא בפני הבית ואמר מורי ה"ר מ"ר דשפיר הם נאכלין אפילו בזמן הזה והא דאמר דאין נאכלין דלא היה להן הנחה לפני הבית והדברים מוכיחין מדפריך עלה מה לבכורים שכן טעונין הנחה והא דמוקי בבכור שנשחט ונזרק דמו לפני הבית אמסקנא דברייתא קאי דמקיש מעשר לבכור ומסתמא בכור דומיא דמעשר דאינו חסר אלא הבאת מקום והיינו כשנזרק דמו לפני הבית אבל ברייתא לא מיירי אלא בבכורים שלא הונחו אבל הונחו לפני הבית אפשר דנאכלין אף לאחר חורבן:
notes.en: Rashi reads thus: “Actually, he holds it did not sanctify for the future.” And it is difficult: if so, why do I need this reason, that the meat is juxtaposed to the blood? Derive it from the fact that it is disqualified by leaving [its area], since [Jerusalem] is like a place that has no wall. And further, it says in Zevaḥim (60a) that if the altar was damaged, one does not eat offerings of lesser sanctity on its account, and derives it from this very reason, that its meat is juxtaposed to its blood; while here it says that this juxtaposition of meat to blood is according to the one who says it did not sanctify for the future. Therefore it seems to the Ri that one reads: “If he holds it did not sanctify for the future, let him not bring second tithe” (with tithe sown before the Temple was destroyed, as we explained), and one reads: “Actually, he holds the initial consecration sanctified for its time and sanctified for the future; and as for your difficulty, let him bring a firstborn too: here we are dealing with one whose blood was sprinkled before the Temple, and the Temple was destroyed, and so on.” Now all the difficulties are resolved. And my teacher examined this: granted, a firstborn whose blood was sprinkled before the Temple is eaten only in the presence of the Temple, as the Gemara explains, because the meat is juxtaposed to the blood; but first fruits that had placement before the Temple, why are they eaten only in the presence of the Temple? And my teacher, Rabbi M. R. [so abbreviated in the text], said that indeed they may be eaten even in the present time, and where it says they are not eaten, it is where they had no placement before the Temple. And the matter proves it, since it challenges: “What about first fruits, which require placement?” And where it establishes the case as a firstborn that was slaughtered and whose blood was sprinkled before the Temple, that refers to the conclusion of the baraita, which juxtaposes tithe to the firstborn; presumably the firstborn is like tithe, which lacks only bringing to the place, that is, when its blood was sprinkled before the Temple. But the baraita speaks only of first fruits that were not set down; if they were set down before the Temple, it may be that they are eaten even after the destruction.

notes.he: אמר רבינא לעולם קסבר קדושה ראשונה קידשה לעתיד ודקאמרת אי הכי אפילו בכור נמי ניתי לא מצית למימר הכי דהכא במאי עסקינן בבכור שנזרק דמו קודם חרבן הבית וחרב הבית ועדיין בשרו קיים ויליף בשרו מדמו מה דמו במזבח אף בשרו במזבח היה צריך מתן (מודסין) [אימורים] במזבח והשתא דליכא מזבח הילכך לית ליה תקנה ולא מצי למיכלה ויליף מעשר שני מהאי בכור דאינו נאכל אפילו בירושלים אף מעשר שני אינו נאכל אע"ג דקידשה נמי לעתיד לבוא ומדמעשר יליף מבכור ק"ו דשאר בכורות ילפי מהאי בכור:
notes.en: [Rabbeinu Gershom’s text reads:] Ravina said: Actually, he holds the initial consecration sanctified for the future; and as for what you said, “if so, let him bring a firstborn too,” you cannot say so, for here we are dealing with a firstborn whose blood was sprinkled before the destruction of the Temple, and the Temple was destroyed, and its meat still exists. And he derives its meat from its blood: just as its blood was at the altar, so its meat at the altar. It required placing [the sacrificial portions] on the altar, and now that there is no altar it has no remedy and cannot be eaten. And he derives second tithe from this firstborn: it is not eaten even in Jerusalem, so too second tithe is not eaten, even though [the initial consecration] sanctified for the future. And since tithe is derived from the firstborn, all the more so are other firstborns derived from this firstborn.

messages.text: Since if the blood is still there and had not yet been sprinkled upon the altar, it is not subject to sprinkling, as the Temple has been destroyed, and consequently the meat of the firstborn offering may not be eaten. This halakha comes and is derived from the halakha of the blood, based upon the juxtaposition in the following verse: “You shall sprinkle their blood against the altar… and their flesh shall be yours”.

verse.he: אַךְ בְּכוֹר־שׁוֹר אוֹ־בְכוֹר כֶּשֶׂב אוֹ־בְכוֹר עֵז לֹא תִפְדֶּה קֹדֶשׁ הֵם אֶת־דָּמָם תִּזְרֹק עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּחַ וְאֶת־חֶלְבָּם תַּקְטִיר אִשֶּׁה לְרֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ לַיהֹוָה׃ וּבְשָׂרָם יִהְיֶה־לָּךְ כַּחֲזֵה הַתְּנוּפָה וּכְשׁוֹק הַיָּמִין לְךָ יִהְיֶה׃
verse.en: But the firstlings of cattle, sheep, or goats may not be redeemed; they are consecrated. You shall dash their blood against the altar, and turn their fat into smoke as an offering by fire for a pleasing odor to GOD. But their meat shall be yours: it shall be yours like the breast of elevation offering and like the right thigh.

notes.he: לעולם קסבר קדושה ראשונה לא קדשה לעתיד לבוא והכא בבכור שנזרק דמו בפני הבית וחרב הבית ועדיין בשרו קיים כיון דאי איתיה לדם אכתי לאחר חרבן [כמו בשר] לאו בר זריקה הוא דליכא בית ההיא זריקה לא חשיבא מידי ואתי (מעשר) [בשר] ויליף מדם מה דם לא חשיבא זריקתו אף בשר נמי לית ליה תקנה ואתי מעשר יליף מבכור ומי ילפינן כו'. ולא מיסתבר לר' האי ל"א אלא אמר דקדמייתא עיקר דהכי אשכחן דכתב במסכת מכות:
notes.en: Another version: actually, he holds the initial consecration did not sanctify for the future, and here it is a firstborn whose blood was sprinkled in the presence of the Temple, and the Temple was destroyed, and its meat still exists. Since, if the blood were still here after the destruction, [like the meat,] it would not be subject to sprinkling, since there is no Temple, that sprinkling counts for nothing; and the [meat] comes and is derived from the blood: just as the blood’s sprinkling does not count, so too the meat has no remedy. And tithe comes and is derived from the firstborn; and do we derive, and so on. And this other version did not seem reasonable to my teacher; rather, he said the first is the main one, for so we find it written in tractate Makkot.

messages.text: This teaches that the meat may be eaten only when the blood is fit to be sprinkled upon the altar. By contrast, there is no such juxtaposition with regard to second tithe, and therefore Rabbi Yishmael remains uncertain whether it may be eaten in the present time in Jerusalem.
And then, as Rabbi Yishmael holds that a firstborn definitely may not be eaten in the present, he says that second tithe comes and its status is derived from the juxtaposition to the firstborn.

notes.he: בהקישא דואכלת לפני ה' וגו' (דברים יד) דמעשר שני איתקש לבכור וכיון דאיכא בכור דפשיטא לו דלא מיתאכיל אלא בפני הבית כגון האי גמרינן מעשר מיניה:
notes.en: And tithe comes and is derived from the firstborn: through the juxtaposition of “And you shall eat before the Lord…” (Deuteronomy 14:23), where second tithe is juxtaposed to the firstborn. And since there is a firstborn about which it is obvious to him that it is eaten only in the presence of the Temple, such as this one, we derive tithe from it.

messages.text: And can we derive the halakhot of sacrificial food from one another?

notes.he: כגון הכא דילפת בשר מדם ומעשר מבשר:
notes.en: And do we derive sacred things from one another? As here, where you derive meat from blood and tithe from meat.

notes.he: והאמר במס' זבחים בכל התורה למידין למד מלמד חוץ מקדשים והאי מעשר ובכור קדשים נינהו ובשרו למוד הוא מדמן והיכא יליף מעשר מבשרו דלמד הוא]:
notes.en: And do we derive sacred things from one another? But it says in tractate Zevaḥim: in the entire Torah we derive a derived thing from a derived thing, except for sacred things. And this tithe and firstborn are sacred things, and its meat is derived from their blood; how then is tithe derived from its meat, which is itself derived?

messages.text: In the entire Torah, we may derive that which is derived from a halakha that was itself derived from another source, except for the case of sacrificial animals, where we do not derive that which is derived from that which was already derived from another source.

notes.he: ומפרש טעמא באיזהו מקומן (זבחים דף מט:):
notes.en: But doesn’t Rabbi Yoḥanan say, and so on: and the reason is explained in Eizehu Mekoman (Zevaḥim 49b).

notes.he: כגון הכא דמעשר למד מבשר ובשר גופיה למד מדם:
notes.en: A derived thing from a derived thing: as here, where tithe is derived from meat, and the meat itself is derived from blood.

messages.text: Second tithe is considered non-sacred. Therefore, this derivation does not pertain to consecrated items.
messages.quote: except for the case of sacrificial animals

notes.he: ולמידין אותו:
notes.en: It is non-sacred: and we derive it.

notes.he: דגן חולין הוא דיכול לחללו ולאוכלו בכל מקום:
notes.en: [Grain] tithe is non-sacred, since one can deconsecrate it and eat it anywhere.

messages.text: This works out well according to the one who said that we follow the halakha that is derived. If it is a consecrated item, it may not be derived from another halakha that was derived from another source, but if it is non-sacred, such as second tithe, it may be derived in this manner.

notes.he: דאם הוא חולין למידין אותו מהמלמד:
notes.en: We follow the derived: if it is non-sacred, we derive it from the teaching source.

messages.text: But according to the one who said that we follow the halakha that teaches, what is there to say? In this case the halakha that teaches, i.e., the source of the derivation, is the meat of the firstborn, which is a consecrated item that is derived itself from the status of the blood of the firstborn.

notes.he: דם המלמד בעי למיהוי חולין:
notes.en: We follow the teaching source: the teaching source must be non-sacred.

notes.he: אי למד קדשים הוא אין למידין מן למד ואי למד חולין הוא למידין מן למד שפיר דמי [דהאי למד מעשר חולין הוא אלא למאן דאמר בתר מלמד אזלינן מאי איכא למימר דמלמד היינו בשרו קודש הוא והיכי מצי יליף מן מלמד דקודש:
notes.en: This works out well according to the one who says we follow the derived: if the derived is a sacred thing, we do not derive from a derived thing; and if the derived is non-sacred, deriving from a derived thing is fine, and this derived thing, tithe, is non-sacred. But according to the one who says we follow the teaching source, what is there to say? For the teaching source is its meat, which is sacred; how can one derive from a teaching source that is sacred?

messages.text: The status of the meat and the blood of a firstborn offering are one matter. Therefore, the meat is not considered as derived from another halakha.

notes.he: הא הוי המלמד בכור. קשיא לי כיון דלא קידשה לעתיד אמאי מספקא ליה במעשר וכמדומה אני שלשון ירושלמי הכתוב בספרים עיקר וכן קבלתי במס' מכות (דף יט.) אי קסבר קידשה לעתיד לבוא בכור נמי ליבעי ואי קסבר לא קידשה מעשר נמי לא ליבעי לעולם קסבר קידשה לעתיד לבוא והכא דפשיטא ליה בבכור כגון שנזרק דמו בפני הבית כו' ול"ג כיון דאם איתיה לדם לאו בר זריקה הוא כו' אלא ה"ג ואתי בשר ויליף מדם מה דמו במזבח אף בשרו במזבח כלומר מה דמו של זה נזרק בזמן מזבח אף בשרו לא יאכל אלא בזמן מזבח ואתא מעשר וגמר מהאי בשר:
notes.en: What is there to say? For the teaching source is the firstborn. It is difficult for me: since [the initial consecration] did not sanctify for the future, why is he in doubt about tithe? And it seems to me that the Jerusalem version written in the books is the main one, and so I received it in tractate Makkot (19a): “If he holds it sanctified for the future, let him be in doubt about the firstborn too; and if he holds it did not sanctify, let him not be in doubt about tithe either. Actually, he holds it sanctified for the future, and here, where the firstborn is obvious to him, it is such as one whose blood was sprinkled in the presence of the Temple, and so on.” And we do not read “since if the blood were there, it would not be subject to sprinkling, and so on”; rather, we read: “And the meat comes and is derived from the blood: just as its blood at the altar, so its meat at the altar.” That is, just as the blood of this one was sprinkled in the time of the altar, so its meat is eaten only in the time of the altar; and tithe comes and learns from this meat.

notes.he: לא הוי הכא למד מלמד דבשר ודם חדא מילתא ומצי יליף מעשר מיניה]:
notes.en: This is not a case of a derived thing from a derived thing, since meat and blood are one matter, and tithe can be derived from it.

messages.text: Rashi, Tosafot and Rabbeinu Gershom each prefer another reading of this passage, in which Rabbi Yishmael holds that the initial consecration did sanctify Jerusalem forever, and the firstborn whose blood was sprinkled before the destruction explains why he is nonetheless certain about the firstborn. Rabbeinu Gershom records the printed reading as another version and gives the preferred answer in Ravina’s name.
One might have thought that a person may bring up a firstborn from outside Eretz Yisrael to Eretz Yisrael when the Temple is standing and sacrifice it.
messages.lead: § The Gemara cites the second statement of Rabbi Yosei from the elders, in the continuation of the baraita above:

messages.text: Therefore, the verse states: “And you shall eat before the Lord your God, in the place which He shall choose to cause His name to dwell there, the tithe of your grain, of your wine, and of your oil, and the firstborn of your herd and of your flock”. Rabbi Akiva derives from here that only from the place that you bring up the tithe of grain to Jerusalem, i.e., from Eretz Yisrael, may you bring up a firstborn to the Temple as an offering.

verse.he: וְאָכַלְתָּ לִפְנֵי ׀ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בַּמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר־יִבְחַר לְשַׁכֵּן שְׁמוֹ שָׁם מַעְשַׂר דְּגָנְךָ תִּירֹשְׁךָ וְיִצְהָרֶךָ וּבְכֹרֹת בְּקָרְךָ וְצֹאנֶךָ לְמַעַן תִּלְמַד לְיִרְאָה אֶת־יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ כׇּל־הַיָּמִים׃
verse.en: You shall consume the tithes of your new grain and wine and oil, and the firstlings of your herds and flocks, in the presence of the ETERNAL your God, in the place where [God] will choose to establish the divine name, so that you may learn to revere the ETERNAL your God forever.

notes.he: מעשר דגן אינו בא אלא מן הארץ בפ"ק דקדושין בסופו (דף לו:):
notes.en: Grain tithe comes only from the Land: in the first chapter of Kiddushin, at its end (36b).

notes.he: וברייתא דלא קיבלו מבית אנטיגנוס ר"ע היא ומתני' רבי ישמעאל היא דלא מייתר ליה האי קרא להך דרשא:
notes.en: You bring up a firstborn: and the baraita that they did not accept from ben Antigonus is Rabbi Akiva’s, and our mishna is Rabbi Yishmael’s, for whom this verse is not free for this exposition.

messages.text: But from a place that you may not bring up the tithe of grain, i.e., outside Eretz Yisrael, you may not bring up a firstborn from there.

Therefore, the statement of the mishna that if one did bring up an unblemished firstborn from outside Eretz Yisrael it may be sacrificed, is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yishmael. By contrast, the statement that ben Antigonus brought firstborn offerings from Babylonia and they were not accepted as offerings is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Akiva.

notes.dh: ממקום שאי אתה מעלה מעשר דגן אי אתה מעלה בכור
notes.he: והשתא אשכחן פלוגתא דרבי ישמעאל ור"ע דרבי ישמעאל אית ליה דלכתחילה אין מביאין בכור ומעשר מחוצה לארץ לארץ אבל דיעבד אם באו תמימים יקרבו והיינו כמתני' ור"ע אפילו דיעבד נמי לא קרבי דאיתקש למעשר דגן וההיא דבן אנטיגנוס כוותיה אתיא וא"ת בשלמא ר"ע כדמפרש טעמא דאיתקש בכור למעשר דגן אלא לרבי ישמעאל מאי טעם אי סבירא ליה היקשא דמעשר דגן אפילו דיעבד נמי לא ואי לא סבר לה אפילו לכתחילה נמי יביא וי"ל דמפיק מדרשא דסיפרי שפירש לעיל רק קדשיך אשר יהיו לך וגו' מכאן שמביאין קדשים מחוצה לארץ לארץ יכול אף בכור ומעשר כן ת"ל רק והיינו דוקא לכתחילה הוא דאימעוט דבהא איירי ביה קרא דכתיב תשא ובאת והיינו לכתחילה:
notes.en: From a place that you do not bring up grain tithe, you do not bring up a firstborn: now we have found the dispute of Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Akiva. Rabbi Yishmael holds that ab initio one does not bring a firstborn and a tithe animal from outside the Land to the Land, but after the fact, if they came unblemished they are sacrificed, which is like our mishna; and Rabbi Akiva holds that even after the fact they are not sacrificed, since it is juxtaposed to grain tithe, and the case of ben Antigonus follows his view. And if you ask: granted Rabbi Akiva, whose reason is explained, that the firstborn is juxtaposed to grain tithe; but according to Rabbi Yishmael, what is the reason? If he holds the juxtaposition to grain tithe, then even after the fact no; and if he does not hold it, then even ab initio let him bring it! One can answer that he derives it from the exposition of the Sifrei explained above: “Only your sacred things which you have…” (Deuteronomy 12:26) — from here that one brings sacred things from outside the Land to the Land. One might think that the firstborn and the tithe animal are the same; therefore it says “only.” And it excludes only ab initio, since that is what the verse speaks of, as it is written: “you shall take and come,” which is ab initio.

messages.text: One might have thought that he may bring up second tithe and eat it in any place that overlooks Jerusalem.
messages.lead: § The Gemara relates the third statement in the baraita, which discusses second tithe:

notes.he: בכל מקום שיוכל לראותו העומד בירושלים:
notes.en: In any place that overlooks: any place that one standing in Jerusalem can see.

notes.dh: יכול יעלה אדם מעשר שני ויאכלנו כו'
notes.he: וא"ת אמאי ס"ד שיהא נאכל בכל הרואה הא לפני ה' אלהיך כתיב ביה וי"ל דומיא דשילה דאוכלים מעשר שני בכל הרואה ויש ספרים דגרסינן לה להך קושיא ולהאי שינויא:
notes.en: One might have thought that a person may bring up second tithe and eat it, and so on: And if you ask: why would we have thought it may be eaten in any place that overlooks? “Before the Lord your God” is written of it! One can answer: like Shiloh, where they ate second tithe in any place that overlooks. And there are books that have this question and this answer in the text.

notes.dh: [בן עזאי אמר יכול יביא אדם מעשר שני
notes.he: בזמן ביהמ"ק ויאכלנו]:
notes.en: Ben Azzai says: one might have thought a person may bring second tithe in the time of the Temple and eat it.

notes.he: בכל מקום שיכול לראות משם ירושלים:
notes.en: In any place that overlooks: in any place from which one can see Jerusalem.

messages.text: But could this matter not be derived through logical inference: A firstborn offering requires that it be brought to the place, i.e., Jerusalem, and a second tithe requires that it be brought to the place. Just as a firstborn animal is eaten only within the walls of Jerusalem, so too, second tithe is eaten only within the walls of Jerusalem.

notes.he: דאינו נאכל:
notes.en: And it is a logical inference: that it is not eaten [there].

notes.dh: מה בכור אינו נאכל אלא לפנים מן החומה
notes.he: דקדשים נפסלין ביוצא:
notes.en: Just as a firstborn is eaten only within the wall: since sacred things are disqualified by leaving [their area].

messages.text: This inference may be refuted: What is unique about a firstborn? It is unique in that it requires the placement of the blood and sacrificial portions upon the altar. Shall you also say that this is the case with regard to second tithe, where that is not required?

notes.dh: מה לבכור שכן חילקת בזמן אכילתו ואוכליו
notes.he: חילקת בזמן אכילתו דאינו נאכל אלא לשני ימים ולילה אחד ומעשר שני לעולם וחילקת באוכליו שאינו נאכל אלא לכהנים ומעשר שני לכל אדם:
notes.en: What about the firstborn, which you distinguished in the time of its eating and in those who eat it? [Rashi’s text of the refutation reads so, where ours has “which requires placing of blood and sacrificial portions on the altar.”] You distinguished in the time of its eating, since it is eaten only for two days and one night, and second tithe forever; and you distinguished in those who eat it, since it is eaten only by priests, and second tithe by any person.

notes.dh: [מה בכור אינו נאכל אלא לפנים מן החומה
notes.he: כדתנן ונאכלים בכל העיר לכל אדם. שכן חלקתה בו זמן אכילתו ואוכלין דבכור תם אינו נאכל אלא לשני ימים ולילה אחד ואינו נאכל אלא לכהנים ומעשר שני אין בו זמן ונאכל לכל אדם:
notes.en: Just as a firstborn is eaten only within the wall, as we learned: and they are eaten throughout the city by any person. [Rabbeinu Gershom, like Rashi, reads the refutation:] Since you distinguished in it the time of its eating and those who eat it: for an unblemished firstborn is eaten only for two days and one night, and is eaten only by priests, while second tithe has no time limit and is eaten by any person.

messages.text: Therefore, the verse states: “And you shall eat before the Lord your God, in the place which He shall choose to cause His name to dwell there, the tithe of your grain, of your wine, and of your oil, and the firstborn of your herd and of your flock.” The verse juxtaposes second tithe and the firstborn, to teach that just as the firstborn is eaten only within the walls, so too, second tithe is eaten only within the walls.

verse.he: וְאָכַלְתָּ לִפְנֵי ׀ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בַּמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר־יִבְחַר לְשַׁכֵּן שְׁמוֹ שָׁם מַעְשַׂר דְּגָנְךָ תִּירֹשְׁךָ וְיִצְהָרֶךָ וּבְכֹרֹת בְּקָרְךָ וְצֹאנֶךָ לְמַעַן תִּלְמַד לְיִרְאָה אֶת־יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ כׇּל־הַיָּמִים׃
verse.en: You shall consume the tithes of your new grain and wine and oil, and the firstlings of your herds and flocks, in the presence of the ETERNAL your God, in the place where [God] will choose to establish the divine name, so that you may learn to revere the ETERNAL your God forever.

messages.caption: One verse, four teachings: what Rabbi Yishmael, Rabbi Akiva, ben Azzai and the “others” each learn from Deuteronomy 14:23.

messages.text: What is difficult for ben Azzai that prompted him to say: One might have thought that it is permitted to eat second tithe in any place that overlooks Jerusalem? You can say that it is difficult for him

notes.he: לבן עזאי דקאמר יכול כו' ומנא תיתי לך האי דיאכל בכל הרואה דאיצטריך קרא להכי:
notes.en: And what is difficult for him: for ben Azzai, who says “one might have thought,” and so on. And where would you get this idea, that it may be eaten in any place that overlooks, that a verse was needed for it?

notes.he: כלומר אמאי בו סלקא דעתין דמעשר יאכל בכל הרואה הכי קשיא ליה משום]:
notes.en: And what is difficult, that we say “one might have thought”? That is, why would it enter our minds that tithe may be eaten in any place that overlooks? This is difficult for him because:

messages.text: The difference between the Tabernacle in Shiloh and the Temple in Jerusalem is only that in Shiloh one eats offerings of lesser sanctity, e.g., individual peace offerings, thanks offerings, and the Paschal lamb, and also the second tithe, in any place that overlooks Shiloh, but in Jerusalem one eats those consecrated items only within the walls.

notes.he: וקשיא ליה בשלמא קדשים קלים בעו מתן דם אלא מעשר ליתאכיל בכל הרואה קמ"ל:
notes.en: And in Jerusalem, within the wall: and it is difficult for him: granted, offerings of lesser sanctity require placing of blood; but let tithe be eaten in any place that overlooks. [The verse] teaches us [otherwise].

notes.he: דהתם נאכל בכל הרואה משום דכפר היה דלית ליה חומה:
notes.en: For we learned: there is no difference between Shiloh, and so on: for there it was eaten in any place that overlooks, because it was an open village that had no wall.

messages.text: And likewise, offerings of the most sacred order are eaten only in the area within the hangings, which surrounded the courtyard in the Tabernacle in Shiloh, which was equivalent to the area within the surrounding wall in the Temple courtyard in Jerusalem.

Lest you say that even in Jerusalem, they may bring second tithe and eat it in any location that overlooks the walls, since, unlike the firstborn animal, second tithe does not possess any unique stringency, the verse teaches us that this is not so, as taught in the mishna.

notes.he: דכתיב ואכלת לפני ה' אלהיך במקום מקודש:
notes.en: Granted, a firstborn requires a wall, since it is written: “And you shall eat before the Lord your God,” in a sacred place.

messages.text: § Rabbi Yosei cites one more statement in the baraita with regard to a firstborn: The mishna (Bekhorot 26b) states that a firstborn animal is eaten from one year to the next, i.e., within its first year, as it is stated: “You shall eat it before the Lord your God year by year”.

verse.he: לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ תֹאכְלֶנּוּ שָׁנָה בְשָׁנָה בַּמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר־יִבְחַר יְהֹוָה אַתָּה וּבֵיתֶךָ׃
verse.en: You and your household shall eat it annually before the ETERNAL your God in the place that GOD will choose.

messages.text: One might have thought that a firstborn whose first year has passed should have the same status as disqualified consecrated animals and therefore be disqualified.

notes.he: מהקרבה הואיל וכתיב שנה בשנה:
notes.en: And be disqualified: from sacrifice, since it is written “year by year” (Deuteronomy 15:20).

notes.he: בכור שעברה שנתו דכתב לפני ה' אלהיך תאכלנו שנה וגו':
notes.en: A firstborn whose year has passed: since it is written: “Before the Lord your God you shall eat it year by year” (Deuteronomy 15:20).

messages.text: Therefore, the verse states: “And you shall eat before the Lord your God…the tithe of your grain, of your wine, and of your oil, and the firstborn of your herd and of your flock.” The verse thereby juxtaposes a firstborn animal to second tithe, which teaches that just as second tithe is not disqualified from one year to the next, so too, a firstborn animal is not disqualified from one year to the next.

verse.he: וְאָכַלְתָּ לִפְנֵי ׀ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בַּמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר־יִבְחַר לְשַׁכֵּן שְׁמוֹ שָׁם מַעְשַׂר דְּגָנְךָ תִּירֹשְׁךָ וְיִצְהָרֶךָ וּבְכֹרֹת בְּקָרְךָ וְצֹאנֶךָ לְמַעַן תִּלְמַד לְיִרְאָה אֶת־יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ כׇּל־הַיָּמִים׃
verse.en: You shall consume the tithes of your new grain and wine and oil, and the firstlings of your herds and flocks, in the presence of the ETERNAL your God, in the place where [God] will choose to establish the divine name, so that you may learn to revere the ETERNAL your God forever.

notes.dh: מה מעשר שני אין נפסל משנה לחברתה
notes.he: שבכל זמן יכול לפדותו ולהעלותו. ותנאי קדמאי ג' זקנים:
notes.en: Just as second tithe is not disqualified from one year to the next: for at any time one can redeem it and bring it up. And the earlier tanna’im are the three elders.

messages.text: And according to the Rabbis, i.e., Rabbi Yishmael, Rabbi Akiva, and ben Azzai, who expound this verse for another explanation, from where do they derive that a firstborn animal is not disqualified from one year to the next?

They derive it from the verse “You shall eat it before the Lord your God year by year.” The formulation “year by year” indicates two years, thereby teaching with regard to a firstborn animal that it is not disqualified from one year to the next.

verse.he: לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ תֹאכְלֶנּוּ שָׁנָה בְשָׁנָה בַּמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר־יִבְחַר יְהֹוָה אַתָּה וּבֵיתֶךָ׃
verse.en: You and your household shall eat it annually before the ETERNAL your God in the place that GOD will choose.

notes.he: שבע שנים במשמע:
notes.en: Year by year: seven years are implied.

messages.text: And according to the opinion of the others, who derive this halakha from the juxtaposition of the firstborn and second tithe, with regard to what do they interpret the verse: “You shall eat it before the Lord your God year by year”? It is necessary for that which is taught in a baraita with regard to the time for the consumption of a firstborn animal:

The phrase “year by year” teaches that there is a manner in which it may be eaten over two years: During one day of this year, and during one day of the next year. The verse therefore teaches with regard to a firstborn offering that it may be eaten for two days and one night in between.

notes.he: ששחטו כמצותו בסוף שנתו וקמ"ל קרא דנאכל אותו יום ויום המחרת שהוא משנה האחרת:
notes.en: One day of this year: that he slaughtered it as commanded at the end of its year, and the verse teaches us that it is eaten that day and the next day, which is of the other year.

messages.text: And the Rabbis, Rabbi Yishmael, Rabbi Akiva, and ben Azzai, from where do they derive the halakha that a firstborn offering may be eaten for two days and one night?

The verse states with regard to the firstborn: “And their flesh shall be yours, like the breast of the waving and the right thigh, it shall be yours”. The repetition of the expression “It shall be yours” teaches that one may eat the firstborn for one more day than a standard thanks offering, which may be eaten only for one day and one night.

verse.he: וּבְשָׂרָם יִהְיֶה־לָּךְ כַּחֲזֵה הַתְּנוּפָה וּכְשׁוֹק הַיָּמִין לְךָ יִהְיֶה׃
verse.en: But their meat shall be yours: it shall be yours like the breast of elevation offering and like the right thigh.

notes.he: דהיינו חזה ושוק של שלמים נאכלין לב' ימים ולילה אחד. [ל"א] יהיה ובשרם יהיה לך כחזה התנופה דמסתמא הוי אזלינן לחומרא ואמרינן (זבחים דף נז.) כחזה ושוק של תודה וכתיב יהיה להוסיף עוד הוייה אחרת כיוצא בה והיינו יום ב':
notes.en: Like the breast of the waving: that is, the breast and thigh of peace offerings, which are eaten for two days and one night. [Another version:] “It shall be… and their meat shall be yours, like the breast of the waving”: for presumably we would go to the stringent side and say (Zevaḥim 57a) “like the breast and thigh of the thanks offering,” and it is written “it shall be” to add another “being” like it, and that is the second day.

notes.he: דנאכל לב' ימים ולילה אחד מן אך בכור שור וגו' וסמיך ובשרם יהיה לך כחזה התנופה וכשוק הימין ואמרינן במס' בכורות ואימא כחזה ושוק דתודה דנאכל ליום ולילה להכי [הדר] כתב בסופיה לך יהיה דאוסיף לך הכתוב הוייה אחד יום שני מכאן שנאכל לשני ימים ולילה אחד:
notes.en: They derive [that it is eaten for two days and one night] from “But the firstborn of an ox…” (Numbers 18:17), and next to it, “And their meat shall be yours, like the breast of the waving and like the right thigh” (Numbers 18:18). And we say in tractate Bekhorot: then say “like the breast and thigh of the thanks offering,” which is eaten for a day and a night; that is why at its end it [again] writes “it shall be yours,” for the verse added for you one more “being,” a second day. From here, that it is eaten for two days and one night.

notes.he: סליק פירקא
notes.en: The chapter is concluded.

messages.text: הדרן עלך אלו קדשים · Hadran alakh Elu Kodashim: we will return to you, chapter 3, “These Are the Sacrificial Animals.”
Chapter 4 · ולד חטאת · Vlad Ḥatat: the five sin offerings that are left to die, beginning with the offspring of a sin offering.
Mishna
The offspring of a sin offering and the substitute for a sin offering, and a sin offering whose owner has died shall be sequestered and left to die.

notes.he: ושעיברה שנתה או שאבדה. אם לא הספיק להקריבה [עד שעיברה שנתה או] עד שאבדה ונמצאת בעל מום או עד משכפרה (בעלמא) [בעליה] באחרת בין זו ובין זו תמות:
notes.en: The offspring of a sin offering, and so on, and one whose year passed or that was lost: if he did not manage to sacrifice it [until its year passed, or] until it was lost and found blemished, or until its owner achieved atonement with another, in either case it shall die.

messages.text: And with regard to a sin offering that is unfit for sacrifice because its first year from birth has passed, and a sin offering that was lost and when it was found, it was blemished, if it was after the owner achieved atonement through sacrifice of another animal as a sin offering, the blemished animal shall die, and it does not render a non-sacred animal exchanged for it a substitute.

notes.he: קודם שנתכפר באחרת:
notes.en: MISHNA. And that was lost and found blemished: before he achieved atonement with another.

notes.he: אחרי כן באחרת:
notes.en: If the owner achieved atonement: afterward, with another.

notes.he: ואפילו לרבנן דאמרי לקמן ופליגי עליה דרבי דאין חטאת מתה אלא שנמצאת לאחר שכיפרו הבעלים בהא מודו הואיל ואיכא תרתי לריעותא דאבדה ונמצאת בעלת מום. ולהכי נקט בעלת מום דאי תמימה הואיל ונמצאת קודם כפרה אפילו כיפרו הבעלים שוב באחרת רועה:
notes.en: It shall die: even according to the Rabbis, who say below, disagreeing with Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], that a sin offering dies only when it is found after the owner achieved atonement, in this case they agree, since there are two detriments: it was lost and it was found blemished. And that is why it mentions “blemished”: for if it were unblemished, since it was found before atonement, even if the owner later achieved atonement with another, it grazes.

notes.dh: מתני' ולד חטאת ושאבדה ונמצאת בעלת מום
notes.he: פרש"י ואפילו לרבנן דאמרי לקמן ופליגי עליה דרבי דאין חטאת מתה אלא בשנמצאת אחר שנתכפרו הבעלים בהא מודו הואיל ואיכא תרתי לריעותא דאבדה ונמצאת בעלת מום ולהכי נקט בעלת מום דאי תמימה הואיל ונמצאת קודם כפרה אפילו כיפרו בעלים שוב באחרת רועה עכ"ל ולא נהירא דמשמע לפירושו דריבוי ריעותא מביאין אותה למיתה ואדרבה סוגיא דשמעתין משמע דריבוי ריעותא מביאין אותה לידי רעייה דאמר רבא בגמ' אבודת לילה לא שמה אבודה פי' ואינה מתה אלא רועה ועוד לר' אבא דאמר בגמ' לקמן (תמורה כג.) הכל מודים שאם נתכפר בשאינה אבודה [אבודה] מתה והכא בנתכפר בשאינה אבודה מיירי וא"כ למה לי בעלת מום לר' אבא מיהו איכא סוגיות בפ' מי שהיה טמא (פסחים דף צז.) ובפ' התודה (מנחות דף פ.) ולקמן (תמורה דף כג.) נמי דלית להו דרבי אבא ועוד דדייק לקמן בגמ' מבבא דמתני' דאח"כ דמתניתין רבנן היא מהכא הוה מצי למידק מדנקט בעלת מום לכ"נ לפרש דנקט בעלת מום לרבותא דמהו דתימא הואיל ואיתרבו כל כך דאבודה ובעלת מום הויא לה כאבודת לילה ורועה קמ"ל דאפ"ה מתה:
notes.en: MISHNA. The offspring of a sin offering… and that was lost and found blemished: Rashi explained: even according to the Rabbis, who say below, disagreeing with Rabbi, that a sin offering dies only when found after the owner achieved atonement, here they agree, since there are two detriments, lost and found blemished; and that is why it mentions “blemished,” for if unblemished, since it was found before atonement, even if the owner later achieved atonement with another, it grazes. End of his words. And this is not clear, for his explanation implies that more detriments bring it to death, while on the contrary the discussion in our Gemara implies that more detriments bring it to grazing, as Rava says in the Gemara: an animal lost at night is not considered lost, meaning it does not die but grazes. And further, according to Rabbi Abba, who says in the Gemara below (Temurah 23a) that all agree that if he achieved atonement with one that was not lost, the lost one dies — and here it deals with one who achieved atonement with one that was not lost — if so, why do I need “blemished” according to Rabbi Abba? However, there are discussions in the chapter Mi SheHaya Tamei (Pesaḥim 97a), in the chapter HaToda (Menaḥot 80a), and below too (Temurah 23a) that do not hold like Rabbi Abba. And further, the Gemara below infers from the next clause of the mishna that the mishna is the Rabbis’; it could have inferred it from here, from its mentioning “blemished.” Therefore it seems to explain that it mentions “blemished” to teach a novelty: lest you say that since it was so diminished, both lost and blemished, it is like an animal lost at night and it grazes, it teaches us that even so it dies.

notes.he: למר כדאית ליה ולמר כדאית ליה לרבי אפילו אם נמצאת לפני כפרה ולרבנן בנמצאת לאחר כפרה:
notes.en: If the owner achieved atonement, it shall die: each master according to his view: according to Rabbi, even if it was found before atonement; according to the Rabbis, when it was found after atonement.

notes.he: זו שנמצאת דלא קדשה קדושת הגוף אלא קדושת דמים:
notes.en: And they do not render a substitute: this one that was found, since it was sanctified not with inherent sanctity but with sanctity of value.

messages.text: Continues on 22a: the mishna goes on: one may not derive benefit from these sin offerings ab initio, but after the fact there is no liability for misuse; and if the lost animal was found before the owner achieved atonement, it grazes until it becomes blemished and is sold.
